item.title: Comfort or Skills at the Start of Your Career?
item.description:
This post is part of the “Before Choosing a Profession” series I created on career choice and planning. All parts of the series: Career

The skills and certifications you acquire at the beginning of your career are crucial for your future life.

I watched a video on YouTube by Serkan Ünal about this, and I highly recommend it to young people. What he explained was this: at the start of your career, you could work a steady job with comfortable conditions and perhaps a better salary compared to your friends. But then your future growth remains within certain standard limits. If you work harder at the start of your career, putting in more effort than your peers to gain more skills, certifications, and competencies, these will pay off in the later stages of your career in terms of salary and position.

item.title: 4 Criteria for Evaluating a Career
item.description:
This post is part of my “Before Choosing a Career” series on career choice and career planning. All parts of the series: Career

You’ve built your profile, and there are a few professions that appeal to you. Now you need to evaluate these careers. I suggest looking at four criteria.

1. How in-demand will it be in the future?
#

This is the first thing everyone looks at, and rightfully so. What will become of this profession in the future, and what are your chances of finding a job in this field? There are forecasts and studies online about how much demand a profession will see in the future. You need to find and evaluate them, using them as one of your criteria.
